extracted.intended_audience: new peer reviewers for PLOS journals / journal article peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist-style guidance for conducting and writing peer reviews of journal manuscripts, aimed at new reviewers. Covers actions to take when invited, reading the manuscript, and composing the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm the manuscript is in your area of expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm the manuscript is in your area of expertise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you have the subject-matter knowledge to judge the work accurately before accepting the invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make sure you have enough time
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you have enough time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess your availability to complete a thorough review within the journal's deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for competing interests
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any conflicts of interest (financial, personal, professional) that would bias your review and disclose or decline as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the research question and key claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the research question and key claims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine what the paper sets out to answer and what the authors claim to have shown; use this as the reference for evaluating coherence and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think about context and related literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Think about context and related literature
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the manuscript situates itself appropriately within existing work, cites relevant literature, and contributes new understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess figures and tables for clarity and representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Look at the figures and tables. Are they clear? Do they represent what the study is about?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether visual elements are understandable, accurately labeled, and appropriately reflect the underlying data and key messages of the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine whether results are supported by the data
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the results. Are they supported by the data?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that analyses, statistics, and reported results follow from the data and are presented transparently; flag unsupported or overreaching claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate whether conclusions are sensible
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the conclusions. Do they make sense?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the conclusions follow from the results, avoid overstating implications, and appropriately acknowledge limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check methods for appropriateness and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the methods. Are they appropriate and reproducible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess study design, experimental or analytical procedures, and reporting detail sufficient for replication; note missing information or methodological flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review the journal guidelines and publication criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the journal guidelines and publication criteria
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the manuscript adheres to the journal's scope, formatting, ethical, and data-sharing requirements; advise authors of any noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep everything confidential!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share manuscript content, ideas, or data with others; respect the review process and authors' unpublished work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start the review with a summary of the research
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a summary of the research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin your review by succinctly restating the study's question, approach, and main findings to show you understood the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: State your overall impression
rubrics_metrics.description: State your overall impression
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, high-level evaluation (e.g., accept, minor/major revision, reject) and the main reasons supporting that view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number comments and separate major and minor issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Number your comments and separate them into “major” and “minor” issues
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize feedback clearly so editors/authors can prioritize; major issues affect validity/acceptance, minor issues are clarifications or small fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give concrete examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Give concrete examples
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support critiques with specific examples from the manuscript (quotations, figure references) and, when possible, suggest concrete remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to specific sections and page numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to specific sections and page numbers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite exact locations in the manuscript to make it easy for authors to find and address points you raise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't focus on spelling and grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t focus on spelling and grammar
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize substantive scientific content and methodological issues over copy-editing; minor language issues can be noted but are lower priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be professional and respectful
rubrics_metrics.description: Be professional and respectful
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write critiques in a constructive, courteous tone; avoid ad hominem language and harsh or dismissive remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate availability to review revised version
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if you’re available to look at the revised version
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell the editor whether you are willing/able to re-review a revision, which helps with editorial planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include positive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Include positive feedback too!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight strengths as well as weaknesses to give balanced, useful feedback to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish on time
rubrics_metrics.description: Finish on time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the review by the deadline to keep the editorial process moving and respect authors' time.
